claim: Plk1 mRNA levels were transiently up-regulated after muscle injury, reaching peak expression levels at 3 days post injury (DPI) and returning to the preinjury levels at 10 DPI.
source: The mRNA levels of Plk1, Plk3, and Plk4 were all transiently up-regulated after muscle injury, reaching peak expression levels at 3 DPI and returning to the preinjury levels at 10 DPI, but Plk1 exhibited the most prominent fold change (increased by >13 fold) at 3 DPI (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1A measuring mRNA levels at various timepoints during CTX-induced muscle regeneration.

claim: Plk1 exhibited the most prominent fold change (increased by >13 fold) at 3 DPI compared to other Plk family members.
source: The mRNA levels of Plk1, Plk3, and Plk4 were all transiently up-regulated after muscle injury, reaching peak expression levels at 3 DPI and returning to the preinjury levels at 10 DPI, but Plk1 exhibited the most prominent fold change (increased by >13 fold) at 3 DPI (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data comparing expression levels of different Plk family members during muscle regeneration.

claim: The expression pattern of Plk1 corresponded to those of myogenic transcriptional factors Pax7 and MyoG at both mRNA and protein levels.
source: The expression pattern of Plk1 corresponded to those of myogenic transcriptional factors Pax7 and MyoG at both mRNA (Figure 1B) and protein (Figure 1C) levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data (Figure 1B) and Western blot analysis (Figure 1C) showing parallel expression patterns.

claim: Plk1 and Plk4 exhibited the most robust down-regulation during myogenic differentiation of primary myoblasts.
source: Compared with day 0 (proliferating myoblast), Plk1, Plk3, and Plk4 levels were all down-regulated during myogenic differentiation (Figure 1D). Among these, Plk1 and Plk4 exhibited the most robust down-regulation (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D measuring mRNA levels during primary myoblast differentiation.

claim: The expression pattern of Plk1 was inversely correlated to the expression of myogenic differentiation markers Myog and eMyhc.
source: The expression pattern of Plk1 was inversely correlated to the expression of myogenic differentiation makers Myog and eMyhc, which were robustly upregulated during differentiation (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1E comparing Plk1 expression with differentiation markers.

claim: Plk1 levels progressively declined from embryonic day 17.5 (E17.5) to postnatal day 90 (P90) during limb muscle differentiation and maturation in vivo.
source: Consistently, Plk1 levels progressively declined from embryonic day 17.5 (E17.5) to postnatal day 90 (P90) during limb muscle differentiation and maturation in vivo (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR analysis shown in Figure 1F measuring Plk1 expression at different developmental stages.

claim: Plk1 immunofluorescence signal was undetectable in any Pax7+ MuSCs in freshly isolated EDL myofibers (Day 0).
source: In the freshly isolated EDL myofibers (Day 0) carrying quiescent MuSCs, Plk1 immunofluorescence signal was undetectable in any Pax7+ MuSCs (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 2A of Plk1 and Pax7 in freshly isolated myofibers.

claim: Plk1 signal appeared in activated MuSCs that co-express MyoD after culture (Day 1).
source: After culture, Plk1 signal appeared in activated MuSCs that co-express MyoD (Day 1), and then was abundantly expressed in clusters of MuSCs progenies or myoblasts (Days 2–3), with positive signal only detected in MyoD+ cells (Figure 2A, n > 200 cells), which marks activated MuSCs (Olguin and Olwin, 2004; Zammit et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 2A and references to established literature on MyoD as a marker of activated MuSCs.

claim: Plk1 was abundantly expressed in clusters of MuSCs progenies or myoblasts (Days 2–3), with positive signal only detected in MyoD+ cells.
source: After culture, Plk1 signal appeared in activated MuSCs that co-express MyoD (Day 1), and then was abundantly expressed in clusters of MuSCs progenies or myoblasts (Days 2–3), with positive signal only detected in MyoD+ cells (Figure 2A, n > 200 cells), which marks activated MuSCs (Olguin and Olwin, 2004; Zammit et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 2A analyzing over 200 cells.

claim: MyoD marks activated MuSCs.
source: After culture, Plk1 signal appeared in activated MuSCs that co-express MyoD (Day 1), and then was abundantly expressed in clusters of MuSCs progenies or myoblasts (Days 2–3), with positive signal only detected in MyoD+ cells (Figure 2A, n > 200 cells), which marks activated MuSCs (Olguin and Olwin, 2004; Zammit et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to established literature (Olguin and Olwin, 2004; Zammit et al., 2004).

claim: Plk1 mRNA level was 15-fold higher in activated than in quiescent MuSCs.
source: Plk1 mRNA level was 15-fold higher in activated than in quiescent MuSCs (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2B comparing FACS-purified quiescent and activated MuSCs.

claim: bFGF increased the level of Plk1 in cultured myoblasts.
source: Additionally, bFGF, a growth factor known to promote the proliferation of MuSCs, increased the level of Plk1 in cultured myoblasts (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C comparing myoblasts treated with or without bFGF.

claim: bFGF is a growth factor known to promote the proliferation of MuSCs.
source: Additionally, bFGF, a growth factor known to promote the proliferation of MuSCs, increased the level of Plk1 in cultured myoblasts (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about bFGF function.

claim: Plk1 expression is dynamically regulated in MuSCs during their quiescence, activation, proliferation and differentiation.
source: Collectively, these lines of evidence demonstrate that Plk1 expression is dynamically regulated in MuSCs during their quiescence, activation, proliferation and differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: No live Plk1MKO pups were obtained after several intercrosses of heterozygous mice.
source: After several intercrosses of heterozygous mice, no live Plk1MKO pups were obtained, indicating that myoblast-specific knockout of Plk1 resulted in prenatal lethality.
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data from MyodCre::Plk1f/f mice.

claim: Myoblast-specific knockout of Plk1 resulted in prenatal lethality.
source: After several intercrosses of heterozygous mice, no live Plk1MKO pups were obtained, indicating that myoblast-specific knockout of Plk1 resulted in prenatal lethality.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the absence of live Plk1MKO pups.

claim: From 69 embryos analyzed at E16.5, 13 motionless embryos were confirmed by PCR to be Plk1MKO.
source: From 69 embryos analyzed, we obtained 13 motionless embryos that were subsequently confirmed by PCR to be Plk1MKO (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by embryo analysis and PCR genotyping data.

claim: Plk1MKO embryos were shorter in body length and transparent in appearance.
source: Plk1MKO embryos were shorter in body length and transparent in appearance (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by visual observation and imaging shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Histological sections through limbs revealed an absence of central-nucleated myofibers in the Plk1MKO embryos.
source: Histological sections through limbs revealed an absence of central-nucleated myofibers that were otherwise stained by eosin and embryonic myosin heavy chain (eMyHC) in the Plk1MKO embryos (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining and eMyHC immunofluorescence shown in Figures 3C-D.

claim: Eosin and eMyHC staining reveals the development of various groups of muscles in the WT control embryos.
source: In contrast, eosin and eMyHC staining reveals the development of various groups of muscles in the WT control embryos (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological staining shown in Figures 3C-D.

claim: Numerous Pax7+ myoblasts were detected in the WT control limb muscles.
source: Whereas numerous Pax7+ myoblasts were detected in the WT control limb muscles, the Plk1MKO limb muscles were completely depleted of Pax7+ myoblasts (Figure 3E), suggesting that Plk1 is necessary for the generation or maintenance of embryonic myoblasts in the limb muscles.
evidence: The claim is supported by Pax7 immunofluorescence shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The Plk1MKO limb muscles were completely depleted of Pax7+ myoblasts.
source: Whereas numerous Pax7+ myoblasts were detected in the WT control limb muscles, the Plk1MKO limb muscles were completely depleted of Pax7+ myoblasts (Figure 3E), suggesting that Plk1 is necessary for the generation or maintenance of embryonic myoblasts in the limb muscles.
evidence: The claim is supported by Pax7 immunofluorescence shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Plk1 is necessary for the generation or maintenance of embryonic myoblasts in the limb muscles.
source: Whereas numerous Pax7+ myoblasts were detected in the WT control limb muscles, the Plk1MKO limb muscles were completely depleted of Pax7+ myoblasts (Figure 3E), suggesting that Plk1 is necessary for the generation or maintenance of embryonic myoblasts in the limb muscles.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the depletion of Pax7+ myoblasts in Plk1MKO embryos.

claim: No Ki67+ cells were Pax7+ in the Plk1MKO limb muscles.
source: In addition, no Ki67+ cells were Pax7+ in the Plk1MKO limb muscles (Figure 3E), suggesting that proliferative failure may be another driver of the depletion of myoblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 and Pax7 co-immunofluorescence shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Proliferative failure may be another driver of the depletion of myoblasts in Plk1MKO limb muscles.
source: In addition, no Ki67+ cells were Pax7+ in the Plk1MKO limb muscles (Figure 3E), suggesting that proliferative failure may be another driver of the depletion of myoblasts.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference from the absence of Ki67+Pax7+ cells.

claim: Loss of Plk1 in myogenic progenitors blocks their proliferation and survival, leading to failure in skeletal muscle development and embryonic lethality.
source: These results indicate that loss of Plk1 in myogenic progenitors blocks their proliferation and survival, leading to failure in skeletal muscle development and embryonic lethality.
evidence: The claim is an inference from multiple observations including depletion of myoblasts, lack of muscle fibers, and prenatal lethality.

claim: The number of MuSCs (Pax7+/DAPI+) in Plk1PKO mice was ~70% of that in WT mice at Day 14 after TMX-induced deletion of Plk1.
source: Immunofluorescence staining of Pax7 showed that the number of MuSCs (Pax7+/DAPI+) in Plk1PKO mice was ~70% of that in WT mice, and no MyoG+ differentiated cells were observed in either WT or KO muscles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of Pax7+ cells shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E-G.

claim: No MyoG+ differentiated cells were observed in either WT or Plk1PKO muscles at Day 14 after TMX-induced deletion of Plk1 in the absence of injury.
source: Immunofluorescence staining of Pax7 showed that the number of MuSCs (Pax7+/DAPI+) in Plk1PKO mice was ~70% of that in WT mice, and no MyoG+ differentiated cells were observed in either WT or KO muscles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by MyoG immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The loss of Plk1 does not lead to obvious morphological changes in uninjured muscles.
source: These results confirm the efficiency of the Plk1PKO conditional KO mouse model and demonstrate that the loss of Plk1 do not lead to obvious morphological changes in uninjured muscles.
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining and fiber area measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: At 7 DPI, the masses of WT TA muscles were recovered to 70% of preinjury levels.
source: At 7 DPI, the masses of WT TA muscles were recovered to 70% of preinjury levels, whereas the TA muscle masses of Plk1PKO mice were only recovered by ~40% (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: At 7 DPI, the TA muscle masses of Plk1PKO mice were only recovered by ~40% of preinjury levels.
source: At 7 DPI, the masses of WT TA muscles were recovered to 70% of preinjury levels, whereas the TA muscle masses of Plk1PKO mice were only recovered by ~40% (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: WT TA muscles were uniformly replaced by newly regenerated myofibers characterized by central-nucleated myofibers at 7 DPI.
source: Histologically, the WT TA muscles were uniformly replaced by newly regenerated myofibers characterized by central-nucleated myofibers (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4D.

claim: TA muscles of Plk1PKO mice were devoid of newly regenerated myofibers at 7 DPI.
source: In contrast, TA muscles of Plk1PKO mice were devoid of newly regenerated myofibers (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Pax7+ cells were diminished in Plk1PKO mice at 7 DPI, together with an absence of any Dystrophin-expressing myofibers.
source: Pax7+ cells were diminished in Plk1PKO mice, together with an absence of any Dystrophin-expressing myofibers (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pax7 and Dystrophin immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4E-F.

claim: Very few MyoG+ cells and no eMyHC+ myofibers were observed in Plk1PKO mice at 7 DPI.
source: Furthermore, very few MyoG+ cells and no eMyHC+ myofibers were observed in Plk1PKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MyoG and eMyHC immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Plk1PKO mice had no Pax7+KI67+ cells at 7 DPI.
source: Compared with uniformly regenerated muscles in WT mice, Plk1PKO mice had no Pax7+KI67+ cells, but a compensatory increase in the number of Pax7–KI67+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D–E), indicating depletion of MuSCs and increased proliferation of non-myogenic cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 and Pax7 co-immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D-E.

claim: Plk1PKO mice had a compensatory increase in the number of Pax7–KI67+ cells at 7 DPI.
source: Compared with uniformly regenerated muscles in WT mice, Plk1PKO mice had no Pax7+KI67+ cells, but a compensatory increase in the number of Pax7–KI67+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D–E), indicating depletion of MuSCs and increased proliferation of non-myogenic cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 and Pax7 co-immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D-E.

claim: The absence of Pax7+KI67+ cells and increase in Pax7–KI67+ cells indicates depletion of MuSCs and increased proliferation of non-myogenic cells.
source: Compared with uniformly regenerated muscles in WT mice, Plk1PKO mice had no Pax7+KI67+ cells, but a compensatory increase in the number of Pax7–KI67+ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D–E), indicating depletion of MuSCs and increased proliferation of non-myogenic cells.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the cell proliferation marker data.

claim: At 21 DPI, the CTX-injured muscles were completely repaired, and the muscle weights were restored to the non-injured levels in the WT mice.
source: To further distinguish if Plk1 KO leads to regenerative delay or deficiency, we examined TA muscles at 21 DPI (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F), at which time the CTX-injured muscles were completely repaired, and the muscle weights were restored to the non-injured levels in the WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2G.

claim: At 21 DPI, the TA muscle mass of the CTX-injured muscles was only 25% of the mass of the non-injured muscles in the Plk1PKO mice.
source: However, the TA muscle mass of the CTX-injured muscles was only 25% of the mass of the non-injured muscles in the Plk1PKO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2G.

claim: Newly regenerated myofibers (indicated by central-nucleation) were uniformly packed in the WT TA muscles at 21 DPI.
source: Newly regenerated myofibers (indicated by central-nucleation) were uniformly packed in the WT TA muscles (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2H.

claim: TA muscles of Plk1PKO mice were devoid of newly regenerated myofibers at 21 DPI, and were infiltrated by Plin1+ adipocytes and F4/80+ macrophages.
source: In contrast, TA muscles of Plk1PKO mice were devoid of newly regenerated myofibers, and were infiltrated by Plin1 +adipocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H–I) and F4/80+ macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining and immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2H-I.

claim: Plk1 KO leads to ablation of MuSCs and severe regenerative failure.
source: These results revealed that Plk1 KO leads to ablation of MuSCs and severe regenerative failure.
evidence: The claim is an inference from multiple observations including depletion of MuSCs, lack of regenerated myofibers, and infiltration by non-myogenic cells.

claim: BI2536 treatment significantly inhibited regeneration of CTX-injured muscles.
source: BI2536 treatment (injection of 50 μl into the TA muscle at a final dosage of 0.4 μg/g body weight) significantly inhibited regeneration of CTX-injured muscles (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: BI2536-treated muscles had increased interstitial space filled with inflammatory infiltration and very few newly regenerated myofibers.
source: H and E staining of vehicle control and BI2536-treated muscle cross-sections revealed that BI2536-treated muscles had increased interstitial space filled with inflammatory infiltration and very few newly regenerated myofibers (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3C.

claim: BI2536 treatment did not have any effects on morphology of uninjured muscles.
source: Consistent to Plk1 KO results, BI2536 treatment did not have any effects on morphology of uninjured muscles (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D), suggesting Plk1 mainly functions to regulate proliferating MuSCs during regeneration.
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Plk1 mainly functions to regulate proliferating MuSCs during regeneration.
source: Consistent to Plk1 KO results, BI2536 treatment did not have any effects on morphology of uninjured muscles (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D), suggesting Plk1 mainly functions to regulate proliferating MuSCs during regeneration.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the observation that Plk1 inhibition affects injured but not uninjured muscles.

claim: BI2536 treatment reduced the number of Pax7+ cells by ~60% in regenerating muscles, but not in uninjured muscle sections.
source: BI2536 treatment reduced the number of Pax7+ cells by~60% in regenerating muscles, but not in uninjured muscle sections (Figure 4—figure supplement 3E–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pax7 immunofluorescence and quantification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3E-F.

claim: BI2536 treatment did not affect the abundance of MuSCs in uninjured EDL myofibers, but significantly reduced the number of MuSCs on CTX-injured myofibers.
source: Similarly, BI2536 treatment did not affect the abundance of MuSCs in uninjured EDL myofibers, but significantly reduced the number of MuSCs on CTX-injured myofibers (Figure 4—figure supplement 3G–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pax7 immunofluorescence on isolated myofibers shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3G-H.

claim: Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of Plk1 similarly inhibits the proliferation of MuSCs and prevents muscle regeneration.
source: These data together suggest that genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of Plk1 similarly inhibits the proliferation of MuSCs and prevents muscle regeneration.
evidence: The claim is an inference from comparing the effects of genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition.

claim: Plk1 expression was significantly increased as cells enter G2 and peaked at metaphase, indicated by phosphohistone H3 (pHH3) labeling.
source: Plk1 expression was significantly increased as cells enter G2 and peaked at metaphase, indicated by phosphohistone H3 (pHH3) labeling (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis of synchronized myoblasts shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The cell-cycle-dependent expression pattern suggests a key role of Plk1 in regulating metaphase progression of MuSCs.
source: The cell-cycle-dependent expression pattern suggests a key role of Plk1 in regulating metaphase progression of MuSCs.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the observation that Plk1 peaks at metaphase.

claim: After 3 days of culture, the WT MuSCs formed clusters of 6–8 myoblasts on the myofibers.
source: After 3 days of culture, the WT MuSCs formed clusters of 6–8 myoblasts on the myofibers.
evidence: The claim is supported by observation of cultured myofibers.

claim: MuSCs from Plk1PKO mice failed to complete the cytokinesis and were arrested at mitosis stage, evident from the dispersed distribution of nuclear Pax7 and MyoD signals surrounding metaphase and telophase chromosomes.
source: However, MuSCs from Plk1PKO mice failed to complete the cytokinesis and were arrested at mitosis stage, evident from the dispersed distribution of nuclear Pax7 and MyoD signals surrounding metaphase and telophase chromosomes (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The numbers of myoblasts were significantly decreased on the Plk1PKO relative to WT myofibers.
source: The numbers of myoblasts were also significantly decreased on the Plk1PKO relative to WT myofibers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Compared to the control (Methanol) treatment in which the number of myoblasts increased exponentially, the numbers of 4-OHT-treated myoblast only slightly increased in the first 12 hr, followed by a gradual decrease.
source: Compared to the control (Methanol) treatment in which the number of myoblasts increased exponentially, the numbers of 4-OHT-treated myoblast only slightly increased in the first 12 hr, followed by a gradual decrease (Figure 5E), suggestive of cell death.
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The gradual decrease in 4-OHT-treated myoblast numbers is suggestive of cell death.
source: Compared to the control (Methanol) treatment in which the number of myoblasts increased exponentially, the numbers of 4-OHT-treated myoblast only slightly increased in the first 12 hr, followed by a gradual decrease (Figure 5E), suggestive of cell death.
evidence: The claim is a speculative inference from the decrease in cell numbers.

claim: The numbers of myoblasts continually decreased when the myoblasts were cultured for more than 2 days after 4-OHT treatment.
source: The numbers of myoblasts continually decreased when the myoblasts were cultured for more than 2 days (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Flow cytometry analyses revealed a significant increase of tetraploid cells 24 hr after 4-OHT induced KO of Plk1.
source: Flow cytometry analyses revealed a significant increase of tetraploid cells 24 after 4-OHT induced KO of Plk1 (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Over 60% of Plk1-null myoblast underwent a cell cycle arrest at M-phase with condensation of the chromatin and the disappearance of the nucleolus.
source: DAPI staining also demonstrated that over 60% of Plk1-null myoblast underwent a cell cycle arrest at M-phase with condensation of the chromatin and the disappearance of the nucleolus (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by DAPI staining shown in Figure 5G.

claim: When EDL myofibers were cultured for 3 days in the absence or presence of 100 nM BI2536, BI2536 treatment not only reduced the total number of myoblast clusters per myofiber by ~70%, but also reduced the number of cells per clusters, with no cluster containing more than four cells.
source: When EDL myofibers were cultured for 3 days in the absence or presence of 100 nM BI2536, BI2536 treatment not only reduced the total number of myoblast clusters per myofiber by ~70%, but also reduced the number of cells per clusters, with no cluster containing more than four cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of myoblast clusters shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: 40% of the vehicle-treated myofibers contained clusters of more than four cells per cluster.
source: In contrast, 40% of the vehicle-treated myofibers contained clusters of more than four cells per cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: BI2536 suppressed the proliferation of primary myoblasts dose-dependently over various timepoints.
source: Consistently, BI2536 also suppressed the proliferation of primary myoblasts dose-dependently over various timepoints (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: More than 40% of the BI2536-treated myoblasts were arrested at an undivided stage, resulting in tetraploid-like cells.
source: Nuclear staining with DAPI indicated that more than 40% of the BI2536-treated myoblasts were arrested at an undivided stage, resulting in tetraploid-like cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C–D), indicating an unsuccessful division of myoblasts by Plk1 inhibition.
evidence: The claim is supported by DAPI staining and quantification shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C-D.

claim: The arrest of BI2536-treated myoblasts at an undivided stage indicates an unsuccessful division of myoblasts by Plk1 inhibition.
source: Nuclear staining with DAPI indicated that more than 40% of the BI2536-treated myoblasts were arrested at an undivided stage, resulting in tetraploid-like cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C–D), indicating an unsuccessful division of myoblasts by Plk1 inhibition.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the observation of tetraploid-like cells.

claim: Loss or inhibition of Plk1 leads to proliferative defect and cell cycle arrest at M-phase.
source: Together, these data reveal a key role of Plk1 in cytokinesis and indicate that loss or inhibition of Plk1 leads to proliferative defect and cell cycle arrest at M-phase.
evidence: The claim is an inference from multiple lines of evidence showing M-phase arrest in Plk1-deficient cells.

claim: 100 mM H2O2 treatment of MuSCs on EDL myofibers cultured for 72 hr resulted in robust C-Cas3 signal.
source: As a positive control, 100 mM H2O2 was used to treat MuSCs on EDL myofibers cultured for 72 hr, which resulted in robust C-Cas3 signal (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: None of the methanol-treated myoblasts on myofibers were C-Cas3 positive.
source: None of the methanol-treated myoblasts on myofibers were C-Cas3 positive, but all the 4-OHT treated MyoD+ myoblasts were C-Cas3 positive at 48 and 72 hr after the treatment (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6A.

claim: All the 4-OHT treated MyoD+ myoblasts were C-Cas3 positive at 48 and 72 hr after the treatment.
source: None of the methanol-treated myoblasts on myofibers were C-Cas3 positive, but all the 4-OHT treated MyoD+ myoblasts were C-Cas3 positive at 48 and 72 hr after the treatment (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The 4-OHT-treated myoblasts were arrested in the cell cycle before the first division.
source: Morphologically, the 4-OHT-treated myoblasts were arrested in the cell cycle before the first division (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological observation shown in Figure 6A.

claim: All activated myoblasts were C-Cas3 negative at 20 hr in both treatment groups, indicative of a cell-cycle-dependent Cas3 activation.
source: All activated myoblasts were C-Cas3 negative at 20 hr in both treatment group, indicative of a cell-cycle-dependent Cas3 activation.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the timing of Cas3 activation relative to cell cycle progression.

claim: MuSCs on EDL myofibers were all TUNEL+ without finishing the first division after 42 hr culture with 4-OHT treatment.
source: In situ terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) also showed that MuSCs on EDL myofibers were all TUNEL+ without finishing the first division after 42 hr culture (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL staining shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Myoblasts cultured from Plk1PKO mice were 100% C-Cas3+ or TUNEL+ when induced with 4-OHT following 2 days of culture.
source: Myoblasts cultured from Plk1PKO mice were also 100% C-Cas3+ or TUNEL+ when induced with 4-OHT following 2 days of culture, but control groups only had ~5% C-Cas3+ or TUNEL+ cells (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence and quantification shown in Figure 6C-F.

claim: Control groups only had ~5% C-Cas3+ or TUNEL+ cells.
source: Myoblasts cultured from Plk1PKO mice were also 100% C-Cas3+ or TUNEL+ when induced with 4-OHT following 2 days of culture, but control groups only had ~5% C-Cas3+ or TUNEL+ cells (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence and quantification shown in Figure 6C-F.

claim: There were no presence of MyoG+ differentiated myoblasts on EDL myofibers from Plk1PKO mice after 72 hr of culture.
source: In addition, there were no presence of MyoG+ differentiated myoblasts on EDL myofibers from Plk1PKO mice after 72 hr of culture (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MyoG immunofluorescence shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Apoptosis of Plk1 null myoblast was confirmed by Annexin V-FITC Apoptosis Staining, which showed a dramatically increment of FITC/PI double positive cells 36 hr after 4-OHT induction when compared to the control group.
source: Apoptosis of Plk1 null myoblast was also confirmed by Annexin V-FITC Apoptosis Staining, which showed a dramatically increment of FITC/PI double positive cells 36 hr after 4-OHT induction when compared to the control group (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Plk1 deletion induced loss of MuSCs due to apoptosis but not differentiation.
source: These results suggest that Plk1 deletion induced loss of MuSCs due to apoptosis but not differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the observation of apoptosis markers and absence of differentiation markers.

claim: Myosin heavy chain (marked by MF20) was observed in 15% of myoblasts treated with BI2536, but rarely observed in control myoblasts cultured in growth media without BI2536.
source: Interestingly, myosin heavy chain (marked by MF20), markers of myogenic differentiation, was observed in 15% of myoblasts treated with BI2536, but rarely observed in control myoblasts cultured in growth media without BI2536 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MF20 immunofluorescence and quantification shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Plk1 inhibition promotes premature differentiation of myoblasts.
